title: DAW Music Production Workflows Core v1

domain.name: DAW Music Production Workflows
domain.description: Cross-DAW production knowledge for FL Studio, Ableton Live, Pro Tools, and comparable systems: session design, MIDI, audio editing, routing, recording, automation, plugins, latency, and delivery.

competencies.name: DAW Sessions, Routing & Signal Flow
competencies.description: Understand tracks, buses, auxes, sends, returns, groups, and master routing across DAWs.
competencies.purpose: Build sessions that remain controllable as production complexity grows.

units.title: Routing expresses signal relationships
units.content: Tracks generate or play signals; buses/groups combine; sends create parallel paths; returns process shared effects; the master represents the final mix path.

units.title: Session routing workflow
units.content: Name and group sources; create logical drum/music/vocal buses; use sends for shared time-based effects; keep gain staging sensible; reserve master processing for intentional mix-bus work; document unusual routing.

units.title: Routing failures
units.content: Avoid feedback loops, hidden double routing, clipping before the master, redundant reverbs on every track, and routing that only makes sense to the original creator.

drills.title: Design a rap session routing map
drills.prompt: Create routing for beat stems, lead vocal, doubles, ad-libs, reverb, delay, vocal bus, instrumental bus, and master.

competencies.name: MIDI, Piano Roll & Sequencing
competencies.description: Edit notes, velocity, timing, controllers, and articulation for programmed instruments.
competencies.purpose: Create expressive programmed performances rather than static note grids.

units.title: MIDI programming workflow
units.content: Choose sound and register; establish core rhythm; edit note lengths; shape velocity; add groove/offset deliberately; automate articulation or CC where supported; humanize only where the musical style benefits.

units.title: Human feel is structured variation
units.content: Random timing is not groove; variation should reflect instrument technique, accent pattern, and musical phrasing.

units.title: MIDI failures
units.content: Avoid identical velocity everywhere, randomization that weakens pocket, impossible instrument ranges, and quantizing expressive parts until phrasing disappears.

drills.title: Program a believable drum groove
drills.prompt: Plan timing and velocity choices for kick, snare, hats, and ghost notes in a hip-hop pattern.

competencies.name: Audio Editing, Time & Pitch
competencies.description: Edit, comp, warp/stretch, tune, and align audio while managing artifacts.
competencies.purpose: Manipulate recordings without damaging timing, tone, or natural phrasing.

units.title: Audio editing workflow
units.content: Preserve originals; comp for performance first; clean boundaries/crossfades; correct timing selectively; choose stretch/warp mode suited to material; tune only what needs correction; review artifacts in context.

units.title: Editing failures
units.content: Avoid hard cuts without fades, excessive time stretching, formant damage, grid-locking every vocal syllable, and destructive edits with no source recovery.

units.title: Correction should protect intention
units.content: Do not remove expressive timing or pitch variation that contributes to the performance.

drills.title: Edit a lead vocal take stack
drills.prompt: Plan comping, timing cleanup, tuning, breath edits, and crossfades for a melodic rap vocal.

competencies.name: Recording, Monitoring & Latency
competencies.description: Set buffer, monitoring, input routing, punch workflow, and recording levels for reliable sessions.
competencies.purpose: Capture performances without distracting latency or clipping.

units.title: Latency is cumulative
units.content: Audio interface buffers, plugins, lookahead processing, software monitoring, and routing can all add delay between performance and monitoring.

units.title: Low-latency record setup
units.content: Set conservative input gain; choose buffer appropriate to the session; bypass high-latency master plugins while tracking; use direct monitoring if suitable; test cue mix and record path; label takes immediately.

units.title: Recording failures
units.content: Avoid tracking through unnecessary lookahead plugins, printing clipping because the beat is too loud, recording to the wrong input, and discovering headphone mix problems after the artist starts.

drills.title: Prepare a vocal tracking session
drills.prompt: Design a low-latency recording setup for vocals over a dense beat.

competencies.name: Plugin Chains & Processing Strategy
competencies.description: Choose EQ, dynamics, saturation, spatial, and corrective processors based on signal problems and goals.
competencies.purpose: Use plugins intentionally instead of accumulating presets.

units.title: Name the problem before the plugin
units.content: If the issue is harshness, masking, unstable level, or lack of depth, define that before selecting a tool.

units.title: Chain design workflow
units.content: Gain stage; fix severe technical issues; shape tone; control dynamics; add character; create space using inserts or sends; level-match when comparing; remove processors that do not improve the mix.

units.title: Plugin chain failures
units.content: Avoid stacking compressors without roles, boosting into clipping, judging louder as better, and copying a chain onto every voice regardless of source.

drills.title: Design a lead-vocal processing chain
drills.prompt: Create a role-based chain for a close rap vocal that needs clarity, control, and depth.

competencies.name: Automation & Arrangement Control
competencies.description: Automate level, pan, effects, filters, mutes, and parameters to support song structure.
competencies.purpose: Make mixes and productions evolve with the arrangement.

units.title: Automation workflow
units.content: Map song sections and energy; identify what should lead each section; automate level and effects to clarify transitions; use filters/throws sparingly; smooth abrupt changes unless intentional; review automation against lyrics and arrangement.

units.title: Automation solves changing problems
units.content: Static plugin settings cannot adapt when the arrangement changes density; automation is part of mixing.

units.title: Automation failures
units.content: Avoid drawing complexity everywhere, overusing delay throws, changing too many parameters at once, and using automation to compensate for a poorly balanced static mix.

drills.title: Automate a chorus lift
drills.prompt: Plan automation from verse to chorus for vocals, music bus, reverb, delay, and stereo energy.

competencies.name: Stems, Consolidation & Cross-DAW Handoff
competencies.description: Prepare sessions and stems so work can move between FL Studio, Ableton, Pro Tools, or collaborators.
competencies.purpose: Preserve timing and intent across different DAWs and plugin sets.

units.title: Cross-DAW handoff
units.content: Set common start point and sample rate; consolidate tracks; print critical sound design or virtual instruments when needed; include dry and processed versions when useful; export tempo map/MIDI if needed; document routing and master processing.

units.title: Handoff failures
units.content: Avoid stems with inconsistent start times, unlabeled alternate versions, missing tempo information, clipping printed stems, and assuming collaborators own the same plugins.

units.title: Print what is essential, document what is optional
units.content: Unique production choices should survive even if the receiving system lacks your plugin.

drills.title: Prepare a cross-DAW handoff
drills.prompt: Define files for moving an FL Studio production into Pro Tools for vocal mix.

competencies.name: Bounce, Stem & Session Delivery
competencies.description: Render mixes, instrumentals, acapellas, stems, and archives with consistent version control.

units.title: Audio delivery workflow
units.content: Confirm approved arrangement; choose bit depth/sample rate for master; export full mix and requested alternates from the same start/end; verify files after bounce; include version/date; archive session plus required assets.

units.title: Delivery failures
units.content: Avoid exporting from different arrangement versions, clipping the bounce, mislabeled clean/explicit versions, and relying on project files that reference missing samples.

units.title: Every deliverable should identify its source state
units.content: Version naming must make it possible to know which session/arrangement produced the file.

drills.title: Prepare a release delivery set
drills.prompt: Plan final mix, instrumental, acapella, performance track, clean edit, stems, and archive.
